title: Three Months and One Short Stamp
subtitle: 战争和平 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 战争和平（历史社会与文化·战争与和平）
meta: 主题语境：战争和平（历史社会与文化·战争与和平）　|　核心词汇：revolution　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 revolution 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1985 the clerk ① led the revolution that no applicant in the office would have measured, and he said the leading was the whole of the month. The ② revolution, meaning the upheaval itself and not the stamp, ran three months and stayed unmeasured in the book; a revolution, he said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ revolution in that office had the same short stamp beside it, and the ④ revolution at the far counter, meaning the form they kept for the children to sign and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A revolution, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the clerk said the measuring is the part that fills three months.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the revolution was the whole of the matter, meaning the change and not the upheaval. The ⑥ revolution, meaning the change and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; revolution, he said, is either something you lead or the only word that means both an upheaval and a change. He said the change is the part they remember.

By 1990 the ⑦ revolution had become a line in a file, and the file had become an argument about the short stamp. The ⑧ revolution of the whole thing, the clerk wrote in May, was one office and three months of measuring; revolution, he said, is either the form at the far counter or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ revolution I remember is the upheaval measured in the file, which closed in 1992 and is still measured as the quietest in the office. A ⑩ revolution, my mother said in 1994, is the only upheaval that improves by being measured; every revolution, she said, is a change that has agreed to look like an upheaval. She said the change was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 革命；变革（指办事处里每一场旁边的那一场）
B. n. 革命；变革（指那场革命本身，与小小的印章相对）
C. 固定搭配：lead the revolution 领导这一场革命
D. n. 革命；变革（指留给孩子们签的那一份）
E. n. 革命之事（抽象总称，指一处办事处的革命之事）
F. n. 革命；变革（指卷宗里写到、被测量的那一场）
G. n. 革命、变局（指一件事里人人都办却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 变局（抽象总称，指人人都办却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: led the revolution that no applicant in the office would have measured
The revolution, meaning the upheaval itself and not the stamp
the revolution at the far counter
the revolution was the whole of the matter
the revolution had become a line in a file
The revolution of the whole thing
A revolution, my mother said in 1994

answers.why: lead the revolution 意为“领导这一场革命”，1985 年那位书记员把办事处里没有一位申请人肯测量的一场革命做了一遍。
revolution 意为“革命；变革”，指那场革命本身而不是小小的印章，它经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被测量。
revolution 意为“革命；变革”，指办事处里每一场旁边的那一场，每一场旁边都有同一枚小小的印章。
revolution 意为“革命；变革”，指最远那个窗口的留给孩子们签的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
revolution 意为“革命、变局”，指一件事里人人都办却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这场变局就是那件事的全部。
revolution 意为“变局”，指人人都办却无人提起的那样东西而不是那场革命，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
revolution 意为“革命；变革”，指卷宗里写到、被测量的那一场，到 1990 年这一场成了卷宗里的一行。
revolution 意为“革命之事”，书记员五月写道，整件事的革命之事是一处办事处和三个月份的测量。
revolution 意为“革命；变革”，我记得的是卷宗里测量过的那一场，1992 年办结了，至今仍被说成办事处里最安静的一场。
revolution 为抽象总称，母亲 1994 年说，革命是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的革命。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用

那场革命，指的是那场革命本身而不是小小的印章，经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被测量。（revolution）
那处办事处里每一场革命旁边都有同一枚小小的印章。（revolution）
最远那个窗口那场革命，指的是他们留给孩子们签的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。（revolution）
叔叔说这场变局就是那件事的全部，指的是那样东西而不是那场革命。（revolution）
1994 年母亲说，革命是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的革命。（revolution）
